question_text: The Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution was passed on:
explanation: Passed at the Minar-e-Pakistan site (then Minto Park), Lahore, during the 27th annual session of the All India Muslim League, 22-24 March 1940. 23 March is observed as Pakistan Day.

question_text: Who presented the idea of a separate Muslim state in his 1930 Allahabad address?
explanation: Iqbal, as President of the Muslim League session at Allahabad (December 1930), envisioned a consolidated Muslim state in north-western India. Rahmat Ali coined the name 'Pakistan' in 1933.

question_text: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was born in:
explanation: Jinnah was born on 25 December 1876 at Wazir Mansion, Karachi.

question_text: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan?
explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan served from 1947 until his assassination at Company Bagh, Rawalpindi, on 16 October 1951.

question_text: Pakistan came into existence on:
explanation: The Indian Independence Act 1947 created two dominions; Pakistan's independence is celebrated on 14 August.

question_text: The national language of Pakistan is:
explanation: Urdu is the national language (Article 251, Constitution 1973); English is the official language.

question_text: The highest peak of Pakistan, and second highest in the world, is:
explanation: K2 stands at about 8,611 m in the Karakoram range. Nanga Parbat (8,126 m) is the second highest in Pakistan.

question_text: Who was the first Governor General of Pakistan?
explanation: Jinnah took oath on 15 August 1947 in Karachi. He was also the first President of the Constituent Assembly (11 August 1947). Mountbatten was the last Viceroy and Governor General of India.

question_text: The All India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at:
explanation: Founded on 30 December 1906 at Ahsan Manzil, Dhaka, during the All India Muhammadan Educational Conference; Nawab Salimullah Khan hosted and Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk was prominent.

question_text: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College at Aligarh in:
explanation: MAO College was established in 1875 and became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

question_text: The Lucknow Pact (1916) was an agreement between:
option_a: Muslim League and the British Government
option_b: Muslim League and the Khilafat Committee
option_d: Indian National Congress and All India Muslim League
explanation: Jinnah played a key role; Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims, earning him the title 'Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity'.

question_text: Jinnah's famous Fourteen Points were presented in:
explanation: They were a response to the Nehru Report (1928) and were presented in March 1929 at Delhi.

question_text: The Cabinet Mission Plan, which proposed a three-tier federation, came in:
explanation: The mission (Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, A. V. Alexander) arrived in March 1946; the plan was announced on 16 May 1946.

question_text: Who chaired the Boundary Commission that demarcated the Punjab and Bengal boundary in 1947?
explanation: The Radcliffe Award was announced on 17 August 1947.

question_text: The Objectives Resolution was passed by the Constituent Assembly in:
explanation: Moved by Liaquat Ali Khan on 7 March and passed on 12 March 1949. It later became the Preamble and, by Article 2A, a substantive part of the Constitution.

question_text: Pakistan's first Constitution came into force on:
explanation: The 1956 Constitution declared Pakistan an Islamic Republic; it was abrogated by Ayub Khan's martial law in October 1958.

question_text: The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was led mainly by:
option_b: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali
explanation: The Ali Brothers led the movement to protect the Ottoman Caliphate; it collapsed after Turkey abolished the Caliphate in 1924.

question_text: The Karakoram Highway connects Pakistan with China through the:
explanation: KKH (Hasan Abdal to Khunjerab, then Kashgar) crosses Khunjerab Pass at about 4,693 m.

question_text: The Lahore Resolution of 1940 was moved by:
explanation: Fazlul Haq (Bengal) moved it; Chaudhry Khaliquzzaman seconded it, supported by leaders from all provinces.

question_text: The first Martial Law in Pakistan was imposed in:
explanation: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution on 7 October 1958 and appointed General Ayub Khan Chief Martial Law Administrator, who removed Mirza 20 days later.

question_text: The Indus Waters Treaty between Pakistan and India was signed in:
explanation: Signed by Ayub Khan and Nehru; the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) went to India, the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan.

question_text: The Tashkent Declaration (January 1966) ended:
explanation: Signed on 10 January 1966 by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri under Soviet mediation.

question_text: The Simla Agreement (July 1972) was signed between:
option_d: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi
explanation: It followed the 1971 war and agreed to settle disputes bilaterally and respect the Line of Control in Jammu and Kashmir.

question_text: The 18th Constitutional Amendment (2010) is best known for:
option_c: Greater provincial autonomy and renaming NWFP as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
explanation: It abolished the Concurrent Legislative List, curtailed the President's powers (including dissolving the Assembly under Article 58(2)(b)), and renamed NWFP.

question_text: The largest province of Pakistan by area is:
explanation: Balochistan covers about 44% of Pakistan's area.

question_text: The national animal of Pakistan is:
explanation: The markhor (screw-horned goat) is the national animal; the Chukar is the national bird and Jasmine the national flower.

question_text: The longest river of Pakistan is:
explanation: The Indus is about 3,180 km long, flowing from Tibet to the Arabian Sea.

question_text: The headquarters of the United Nations is located in:
explanation: The UN HQ is in New York City; the UN was founded in 1945.

question_text: The smallest country in the world by area is:
explanation: Vatican City covers about 0.44 sq km.

question_text: The largest ocean in the world is the:
explanation: The Pacific covers about one-third of Earth's surface.

question_text: The largest hot desert in the world is:
explanation: The Sahara spans about 9 million sq km across North Africa.

question_text: The Pakistan Military Academy (PMA) is located at:
explanation: PMA Kakul was established in 1947 and is Pakistan Army's premier officers' training institution.

question_text: Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests at Chagai on:
explanation: Observed as Youm-e-Takbeer; this followed India's May 1998 tests.

question_text: The International Red Cross movement was founded by:
explanation: Dunant, a Swiss businessman, was the first Nobel Peace Prize winner (1901) and the Red Cross was founded in 1863.

question_text: The Secretariat of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) is based in:
explanation: The OIC was founded in 1969 after the Al-Aqsa arson; its headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

question_text: The SAARC Secretariat is located in:
explanation: SAARC was established in Dhaka in December 1985; its Secretariat is in Kathmandu, Nepal.

question_text: Malala Yousafzai received the Nobel Peace Prize in:
explanation: She shared it with Kailash Satyarthi and is the youngest Nobel laureate.

question_text: Dr. Abdus Salam received the Nobel Prize in Physics in:
explanation: Shared with Sheldon Glashow and Steven Weinberg for the electroweak unification theory; he is Pakistan's first Nobel laureate.

question_text: Pakistan's first satellite, Badr-I, was launched in:
explanation: Badr-I was launched by a Chinese Long March rocket on 16 July 1990 under SUPARCO.

question_text: The headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) is in:
explanation: The WHO was founded on 7 April 1948 and is based in Geneva, Switzerland.

question_text: How many permanent members does the UN Security Council have?
explanation: USA, UK, France, Russia and China hold veto power; there are also 10 non-permanent members, making 15 in total.

question_text: Who became the first woman Prime Minister of a Muslim-majority country?
explanation: Benazir Bhutto first took office on 2 December 1988.

question_text: Gwadar was purchased by Pakistan from the Sultanate of Oman in:
explanation: Gwadar was handed over on 8 September 1958 and became part of Balochistan in 1977; the deep-sea port is central to CPEC.

question_text: The Durand Line, the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan, was drawn in:
explanation: It was agreed between Sir Mortimer Durand (British India) and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan in 1893.

question_text: The Strait of Hormuz connects:
option_a: The Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman
option_b: The Red Sea and the Mediterranean
option_c: The Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal
option_d: The Black Sea and the Aegean
explanation: It lies between Iran and Oman/UAE and carries a large share of the world's seaborne oil.

question_text: The first recipient of Nishan-e-Haider, Pakistan's highest military gallantry award, was:
explanation: Captain Sarwar (Punjab Regiment) was martyred in Kashmir in July 1948; he was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider as the first recipient.

question_text: Pilot Officer Rashid Minhas Shaheed, a Nishan-e-Haider recipient, belonged to the:
explanation: He was martyred on 20 August 1971 while preventing a hijacked T-33 trainer from being flown to India. He is the youngest recipient and the only PAF recipient.

question_text: The lowest point on land on Earth's surface is the:
explanation: The Dead Sea shore is about 430 m below sea level.

question_text: How many Surahs are there in the Holy Quran?
explanation: The Quran has 114 Surahs and 30 Juz (paras).

question_text: The first revelation to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was in the Cave of Hira. It began with Surah:
explanation: The first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq were revealed, in Ramadan, when the Prophet was 40 years old.

question_text: How many pillars (Arkan) of Islam are there?
explanation: Shahadah, Salah, Zakah, Sawm and Hajj.

question_text: The first Caliph of Islam was:
explanation: He ruled 11-13 AH (632-634 CE) and is called 'As-Siddiq'.

question_text: The Hijrah (migration to Madinah) took place in:
explanation: The Islamic (Hijri) calendar starts from this event.

question_text: The longest Surah of the Quran is:
explanation: Al-Baqarah has 286 verses.

question_text: The shortest Surah of the Quran is:
explanation: Al-Kawthar has 3 verses (10 words in Arabic).

question_text: The number of Fard rakats in Fajr prayer is:
explanation: Fajr 2, Zuhr 4, Asr 4, Maghrib 3, Isha 4 (Fard).

question_text: The Battle of Badr was fought in:
explanation: About 313 Muslims faced about 1,000 Quraish and won; the Quran calls it Yaum-ul-Furqan.

question_text: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was signed in:
explanation: A ten-year truce between Muslims and Quraish; the Quran (Surah Al-Fath) called it a 'clear victory'.

question_text: The conquest of Makkah took place in:
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah with 10,000 companions and declared a general amnesty.

question_text: The rate of Zakah on gold, silver and cash savings is:
explanation: Zakah is due on wealth above Nisab held for one lunar year.

question_text: The Nisab of silver for Zakah is:
explanation: Gold Nisab is 7.5 tola (87.48 grams).

question_text: The Hijri calendar was introduced by:
explanation: Umar (RA) fixed the Hijrah as its starting point; the first month is Muharram.

question_text: Which Caliph is known as 'Dhun-Noorain' (Possessor of Two Lights)?
explanation: He married two daughters of the Prophet (PBUH), Ruqayyah and later Umm Kulthum, and also standardized the Quranic text.

question_text: The most authentic collection of Hadith is considered to be:
explanation: Compiled by Imam Muhammad bin Ismail al-Bukhari; Sahih Muslim ranks next.

question_text: The four primary sources of Islamic law (Fiqh) in Sunni jurisprudence are:
explanation: Quran and Sunnah are primary; Ijma (consensus) and Qiyas (analogy) follow.

question_text: Ayat-ul-Kursi is found in Surah:
explanation: It is considered the greatest verse of the Quran according to a hadith.

question_text: The Quran was first compiled in a single book form during the caliphate of:
explanation: After the Battle of Yamama, Zaid bin Thabit compiled it on Umar's suggestion; Uthman later made standard copies (Mushaf-e-Uthmani).

question_text: Which Surah of the Quran does NOT begin with 'Bismillah'?
explanation: Surah At-Tawbah (Surah 9) begins without Bismillah.

question_text: In which Surah does 'Bismillah' occur twice?
explanation: Once at the beginning and once within verse 30 (the letter of Sulaiman, AS to the Queen of Sheba).

question_text: The Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab) was fought in:
explanation: A trench was dug around Madinah on Salman Farsi's suggestion. Uhud was in 3 AH.

question_text: Who is regarded as the first free adult man to accept Islam?
explanation: Khadija (RA) was the first woman, Ali (RA) the first youth/boy, Zaid (RA) the first freed slave.

question_text: The Last Sermon (Khutbah Hajjat-ul-Wada) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was delivered at:
option_b: Mount Arafat on 9 Dhul Hijjah, 10 AH
explanation: It was delivered during the Farewell Pilgrimage in the valley of Uranah at Arafat; it emphasised human equality, the rights of women and the sanctity of life and property.

question_text: The SI unit of force is:
explanation: 1 N = 1 kg m/s2.

question_text: The SI unit of frequency is:
explanation: 1 Hz = one cycle per second.

question_text: The SI unit of power is:
Which of the following is a vector quantity?
explanation: Velocity has both magnitude and direction; speed, mass and temperature are scalars.

question_text: The approximate value of acceleration due to gravity on Earth's surface is:
explanation: g is about 9.8 m/s2 (about 1.6 on the Moon).

question_text: Newton's first law of motion is also known as the law of:
explanation: A body stays at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by a net external force.

question_text: A 12 V battery is connected across a 4 ohm resistor. The current is:
explanation: I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 A (Ohm's law).

question_text: Sound travels fastest in:
explanation: Sound travels at about 340 m/s in air, 1,500 m/s in water and 5,000 m/s in steel; it cannot travel in a vacuum.

question_text: Which type of mirror is used as the reflector in a vehicle's headlight?
explanation: A lamp at the focus of a concave mirror gives a parallel beam. Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors because they give a wider field of view.

question_text: The kinetic energy of a 2 kg body moving at 3 m/s is:
A stone is dropped from rest. Taking g = 10 m/s2, its speed after 5 s is:
Two resistors of 4 ohm and 6 ohm are connected in series. The total resistance is:
explanation: In series, R = R1 + R2 = 10 ohm.

question_text: A force of 10 N acts at 60 degrees to the displacement of 5 m. The work done is:
explanation: W = F d cos(theta) = 10 x 5 x 0.5 = 25 J.

question_text: Which electromagnetic radiation has the highest frequency?
explanation: Order of increasing frequency: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.

question_text: The power of a lens of focal length 50 cm (converging) is:
explanation: P = 1/f (in metres) = 1/0.5 = +2 D.

question_text: Two resistors of 4 ohm and 6 ohm are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is:
For a given speed of projection, the horizontal range of a projectile is maximum when the angle of projection is:
explanation: R = (v2 sin 2theta)/g is maximum when sin 2theta = 1, i.e. theta = 45 degrees.

question_text: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from:
option_a: A denser to a rarer medium at an angle less than the critical angle
option_b: A rarer to a denser medium at an angle greater than the critical angle
option_c: A denser to a rarer medium at an angle greater than the critical angle
option_d: A rarer to a denser medium at any angle
explanation: This is the principle behind optical fibres and diamonds' sparkle.

question_text: Impulse of a force is equal to the:
explanation: Impulse = F x t = change in momentum (Delta p). Rate of change of momentum equals force.

question_text: A 2 kg mass moves in a circle of radius 2 m at a constant speed of 4 m/s. The centripetal force is:
The escape velocity from Earth's surface is approximately:
explanation: Escape velocity = sqrt(2gR) which is about 11.2 km/s; 7.9 km/s is the orbital velocity near the surface.

question_text: The photoelectric effect was explained by Einstein using the idea of:
explanation: Einstein received the 1921 Nobel Prize for this; E = hf = work function + maximum kinetic energy of the electron.

question_text: The time period of a simple pendulum of length 1 m on Earth (g = 9.8 m/s2) is approximately:
explanation: T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g) = 6.28 x 0.32 which is about 2.0 s.

question_text: After three half-lives, the fraction of a radioactive sample that remains undecayed is:
explanation: Remaining fraction = (1/2)3 = 1/8.

question_text: Choose the synonym of ABUNDANT:
explanation: Abundant means existing in large quantities.

question_text: Choose the antonym of ANCIENT:
explanation: Ancient means very old; modern is its opposite.

question_text: He is very good ___ mathematics.
explanation: 'Good at' is the correct collocation for skill in a subject.

question_text: She ___ to school every day.
explanation: Third-person singular simple present takes -s/-es.

question_text: Choose the correctly spelled word:
explanation: Accommodation has double c and double m.

question_text: Choose the antonym of GENEROUS:
explanation: Generous means giving freely; miserly means unwilling to spend or give.

question_text: Idiom: 'A piece of cake' means:
explanation: Used for a task that is effortless.

question_text: He is ___ honest man.
explanation: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (silent h), so 'an' is used.

question_text: Choose the synonym of CANDID:
explanation: Candid means truthful and straightforward.

question_text: Choose the antonym of EXPAND:
explanation: Expand means to grow in size; contract means to shrink.

question_text: Idiom: 'Once in a blue moon' means:
explanation: Used for something that happens extremely seldom.

question_text: One word for 'a person who loves mankind and does good for others':
explanation: A philanthropist works to promote human welfare; a misanthrope hates people.

question_text: One word for 'the scientific study of ancient remains and artefacts':
explanation: Archaeology studies human history through material remains.

question_text: If I ___ you, I would accept the offer.
explanation: In unreal (second) conditional sentences, 'were' is used for all subjects.

question_text: Neither of the boys ___ present in the class.
explanation: 'Neither' takes a singular verb.

question_text: He has been living in this city ___ 2010.
explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time; 'for' with a period (for ten years).

question_text: Change to passive: 'They are building a new bridge.'
option_a: A new bridge was being built by them.
option_b: A new bridge is built by them.
option_c: A new bridge is being built by them.
option_d: A new bridge has been built by them.
explanation: Present continuous passive: is/are + being + past participle.

question_text: Change to indirect speech: He said, 'I am busy.'
option_a: He said that he is busy.
option_b: He said that he has been busy.
option_c: He said that I was busy.
option_d: He said that he was busy.
explanation: Present simple becomes past simple and the pronoun changes in reported speech.

question_text: Choose the synonym of EPHEMERAL:
explanation: Ephemeral describes something lasting a very short time.

question_text: Choose the antonym of BENEVOLENT:
explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and kind; malevolent means wishing harm.

question_text: Choose the synonym of OBSTINATE:
explanation: Obstinate means refusing to change one's opinion or course of action.

question_text: One word for 'one who knows everything':
explanation: Omnipotent = all-powerful, omnipresent = everywhere, omnivorous = eating everything.

question_text: Idiom: 'To bite the bullet' means:
option_c: To face a painful situation with courage
explanation: It means to endure something unpleasant that cannot be avoided.

question_text: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
option_a: Each of the students have completed their assignment.
option_b: Each of the students were completed his assignment.
option_c: Each of the students has completed his or her assignment.
option_d: Each of the students are completing his assignment.
explanation: 'Each' is singular and takes 'has'.
